concept.title: ArrayDeque 向较近端搬移
concept.core_question: ArrayDeque 为什么根据 i 与 n/2 的关系选择搬移方向？
concept.summary: 它只搬移插入或删除位置到较近端之间的元素，把搬移数量限制为 min(i,n-i)。
concept.definition: ArrayDeque 在位置 i 更新时比较 i 与 n/2。若 i 靠近逻辑前端，就调整 j 并搬移前缀；否则搬移后缀。插入与删除采用相反但对称的搬移方向，使被移动元素数不超过 $\min\{i,n-i\}$，忽略 resize 的时间为 $O(1+\min\{i,n-i\})$。

relations.description: 理解《ArrayDeque 向较近端搬移》是继续学习目标知识点的直接基础。

rookie_explanation.analogy: 在一排人中腾出或补上一个位置时，选择让距离该位置更近的一端人群移动，而不是固定让整条右侧队伍移动。

mapping.移动方向: 循环数组中的搬移分支

rookie_explanation.boundary: 类比不展示回绕下标计算，也不包含 resize 的成本。

related_concepts.title: ArrayDeque 的循环数组表示与访问
related_concepts.core_question: ArrayDeque 如何在循环数组中定位任意逻辑下标？
related_concepts.summary: ArrayDeque 复用队首 j 与元素数 n，把逻辑下标 i 映射为 (j+i) mod capacity。
related_concepts.definition: ArrayDeque 用数组 a、逻辑起点 j 和元素数 n 表示 List。逻辑元素 i 存放于 $a[(j+i)\bmod \mathrm{length}(a)]$；get 与 set 直接使用该映射，因此为常数时间。循环布局允许逻辑序列在数组末端回绕。

related_concepts.title: ArrayDeque 的操作复杂度
related_concepts.core_question: ArrayDeque 为什么能在两端附近高效插入和删除？
related_concepts.summary: get/set 为 O(1)，add/remove(i) 为 O(1+min(i,n-i))，容量调整总成本可线性摊还。
related_concepts.definition: ArrayDeque 实现 List 接口时，get 与 set 为 $O(1)$；忽略 resize，add(i,x) 与 remove(i) 为 $O(1+\min\{i,n-i\})$。从空结构开始的 m 次更新中，所有 resize 总时间为 $O(m)$，因此两端位置的更新具有常数摊还时间。

source_records.content: The implementation of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} is a little more interesting. As usual, we first check if \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}}} is full and, if necessary, call \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}} to resize \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}}}. Remember that we want this operation to be fast when \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}} is small (close to 0) or when \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}} is large (close to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}). Therefore, we check if $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}<\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2$. If so, we shift the elements $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[0]}},\ldots,\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}-1]}}$ left by one position. Otherwise ($\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}\ge\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2$), we shift the elements $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}]}},\ldots,\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}-1]}}$ right by one position. See \figref{arraydeque} for an illustration of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} operations on an ArrayDeque.

A sequence of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operations on an ArrayDeque. Arrows denote elements being copied.

By doing the shifting in this way, we guarantee that \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} never has to shift more than $\min\{ \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}, \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}} \}$ elements. Thus, the running time of the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} operation (ignoring the cost of a \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}} operation) is $O(1+\min\{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}},\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}\})$. The implementation of the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operation is similar. It either shifts elements $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[0]}},\ldots,\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}-1]}}$ right by one position or shifts the elements $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}+1]}},\ldots,\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}-1]}}$ left by one position depending on whether $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}<\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2$. Again, this means that \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} never spends more than $O(1+\min\{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}},\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}\})$ time to shift elements.
